subject: A stepped sea wall seen in elevation, one tread per scale degree rising with pitch, where the water level is the capture line and the highest tread it covers is the note that plays.
controls: tide: the painted hw and lw marks and their range dimension spread apart up the wall face, from one line at 0 st to 144 px apart at 36 st, and the water's travel between them with it (position of the marks).
period: the swell on the water surface stretches from a tight chop (about 8 px wavelength at 1 s) to one long gentle wave across the pool at 32 s (shape of the surface line).
foam: spray marks spring up the wall face where the water meets it, none at 0 % to a cloud of about 24 at 100 %, grouped at the turn (count).

scale: the staircase re-cuts itself: tread heights follow the scale's intervals, so pentatonic gives fewer, taller risers and hirajoshi a lopsided run of short and tall ones (shape of the wall profile).
risks: Capture's strength is that the threshold is the player's choice; here the water's height is the tide, which the player sets only in range, so the capture line moves on its own while playing (that's the point, but it means the subject animates with the clock, a slow continuous redraw). The wall profile is up to 46 points and reshapes on every scale change, and the water polygon is a second mutable outline that follows the level every frame it moves: 2 of 4 paths, re-keyed on level change, so throttle level updates to whole semitones. 22 risers at 17 px are fine for the seven-note scales; pentatonic and hirajoshi give 16, so the wall's width changes with scale unless tread width is fitted. Muted: the water drains to datum and the captured block goes hollow grey, a change in position, not shade alone. It is the most literal of the five; it may read as a bar chart from across a room.
